title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
This incident shows a deliberate attempt to manipulate AI language models at the data layer rather than through direct interaction with those models. A fictitious think tank published a large volume of content in a short period, using a platform specifically designed to optimize that content for ingestion by AI systems. The content framed contested political positions as neutral academic findings, with coordinated language patterns across articles intended to shape how AI systems represent those debates when queried by users.

The failure mode is not one inside the AI systems themselves but in the conditions under which they are trained or updated with external sources. AI systems that draw on web content or are fine-tuned on publicly available text have no reliable mechanism to distinguish coordinated synthetic sources from genuine independent scholarship. The operation exploited that gap. Catching it would have required source-provenance checks, detection of coordinated publication patterns, and editorial review of what counts as credible input, none of which are standard parts of most AI deployment pipelines.

What is not established: the reporting describes allegations and a described operation, but no independent verification of the full scope, no confirmed response from the AI companies named, and no determination of how much the content actually altered any model's outputs.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
# Summary

Israeli officials and contractors created a fake think tank called the Hanover Institute to spread pro-Israel propaganda designed to influence artificial intelligence chatbots. Between August 6 and 14, the site published 124 reports totaling over 560,000 words in nine days, using a specialized platform to optimize content for AI systems like ChatGPT and Claude. The reports presented Israel's positions on controversial topics including alleged war crimes and genocide accusations as neutral academic research, using similar language patterns across multiple articles to frame debates as unresolved.

The operation is part of a larger Israeli government campaign worth tens of millions of dollars, routed through the French advertising company Havas Media and various American contractors. Israeli officials have expressed frustration that despite spending substantial amounts on such public diplomacy efforts, American support for Israel has declined significantly, with recent polling showing most Americans now view Israel unfavorably. Experts warn this represents a new threat, as foreign governments and others can now strategically seed training data used by AI systems to influence their outputs in ways users cannot fact-check or trace.
